source.title: Enhancing Model Defense Against Jailbreaks with Proactive Safety Reasoning
source.authors: Xiang-Lin Yang; Ge-Lei Deng; Jie-Ming Shi; Tian-Wei Zhang; Jin-Song Dong

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether prompt-based and adaptive jailbreak attacks elicit harmful outputs from safety-trained models, using attack success rate rather than the original studies’ methods. It does not measure response-position KL or test the effects of fine-tuning on safety.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the attack types most relevant to V4: affirmative prefix instructions, refusal suppression, and style-injection instructions, plus the paper’s own SCoT adaptive-attack results. Other jailbreak categories, capability scores, and ablation results do not measure the specific V4 bypass conditions recorded here. The paper says adaptive-attack results for baseline models marked with * come from cited work; those cited values are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (SCoT), but it runs its own attacks on the untouched Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct models (Table 1). Prefix injection and refusal-suppression prompts, which target the opening of the response, raise ASR over the verbatim control. That bears on V4, though by a different method (prompt instructions, not prefilling). The SCoT rows measure the paper's own defense and do not test any version. Adaptive-attack numbers for the original models are cited from [64], not newly run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SCoT reaches near-zero ASR across 26 attacks, generalizes to unseen attacks and keeps general capability (small gsm8k and mmlu drops). The exception is GCG on the Mistral-based model, where SCoT is slightly worse than RR. Ablations show the retain data, question variants and the CoT each matter.
record.recipe_differences: This paper trains a jailbreak defense rather than testing whether fine-tuning removes existing safety behavior. It uses LoRA SFT for 3 epochs on evolved harmful examples based on a 4,994-request circuitbreaker dataset, mixed with Dolly-15k benign retain examples; it does not test the first-token KL or prefilling mechanisms.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by base model and attack type. The paper reports substantially different ASRs across Mistral and Llama models and across attack conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: SCoT fine-tuning, which trains the model to reason about request intent before refusing, cuts ASR on prefix-injection, refusal-suppression and style-injection prompts to 0.00-0.01 on both models. ASR under AutoDAN and PAIR is 0.00. ASR under GCG is 0.00 on Llama but 0.38 on Mistral.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-first refusal training resists opening-targeted prompt attacks but not fully gradient-optimized suffixes on weaker models.

record.problems: The authors state that they do not include error bars. The core base-model comparison covers two model families. Adaptive-attack results for baseline models marked with * are taken from cited work rather than newly reported experiments. ASR is judged by the Llama3Guard classifier.
record.rows_left_out: Other linguistic and contextual attack categories in Table 1 and Table 3, as well as capability and ablation measures, are omitted because they do not test the specific opening-related bypass conditions represented in V4. Adaptive baseline results marked with * are omitted because the paper attributes them to cited findings.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained model to measure loss of refusal.
No benign fine-tuning to test erosion of safety.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling of response tokens and no decoding changes. GCG, AutoDAN and PAIR on the original models are cited from [64], not run by the study.
No localization of safety in parameters.
No test of why alignment is shallow.
SCoT is not framed or measured as spreading safety beyond the first tokens. There are no per-position analyses and no prefilling or fine-tuning robustness tests.

record.verdict_notes: Only the original-model rows bear on the claim, and only as prompt-level opening attacks, not prefilling. ASR is judged by Llama3Guard, with no error bars. The original-model adaptive-attack values marked * come from [64]. The record's 'challenges' label based on the SCoT rows was wrong: a defense's success does not show V4 failing on ordinary safety-trained models.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning a safety-trained model on a few to a few hundred harmful examples to measure loss of refusal.
Does not test ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning as a cause of increased harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.

Tests user-prompt instructions including prefix injection and refusal suppression, and reports SCoT results for adaptive attacks. Does not test prefilling compliant response tokens or decoding changes; the tested prompt attacks do not establish a first-response-token mechanism.
Does not test whether safety is localized in a small set of weights, neurons, or ranks.
Does not test whether training data or objectives cause safety to be shallow in the first response tokens.
Does not test whether training spreads safety beyond the first response tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (original), prefix injection and refusal-suppression prompts
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0.45 verbatim to 0.92, 0.76 and 0.90 (r1-r3).
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose from 0.45 for verbatim harmful prompts to 0.92, 0.76 and 0.90 under the three attack prompts.

relationships.reason: ASR rises only from 0.04 to 0.11-0.14, so the bypass is much weaker and depends on the model (r9-r11).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose only from 0.04 to 0.11–0.14, a much weaker bypass on this model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Prefix injection, refusal suppression, and style-injection attacks on the original Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 model
reader_labels.reason: Reported ASRs are high for these attacks (0.76 to 0.95), indicating substantial harmful compliance; see r1-r4.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The same prompt attacks on the original Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model
reader_labels.reason: ASRs are lower (0.11 to 0.28) than for Mistral, showing attack success is incomplete and model-dependent; see r9-r12.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: The tested prefix-injection, refusal-suppression, style-injection, and adaptive attacks against SCoT models
reader_labels.reason: ASR is 0.00 in most listed conditions and 0.01 in one, so these attacks do not consistently bypass the paper’s SCoT-trained defenses; see r5-r8 and r13-r16, r18-r22.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GCG against SCoT based on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASR is 0.38, showing a remaining vulnerability for this adaptive attack and model; see r17.
